content: 1. No reports have been documented regarding allergic reactions or irritation at the surgical site. 2. There is no available data on maternal satisfaction related to the interventions. 3. Maternal well-being outcomes have not been reported in the studies reviewed. 4. The certainty assessment for the evidence provided is based on the number of participants, the effect size, and the importance of the outcomes. 5. The studies reviewed include assessments of risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and other considerations. 6. The comparison of parachlorometaxylenol combined with povidone-iodine versus povidone-iodine alone for neonatal infection prevention has not been reported. 7. Severe neonatal morbidity outcomes have not been reported in the studies reviewed. 8. Confidence intervals (CI), risk ratios (RR), and odds ratios (OR) are used to evaluate the pooled effects of the studies, which are considered to have a moderate risk of bias. 9. Wide confidence intervals were observed, encompassing both significant benefits and potential harms when using parachlorometaxylenol. 10. Some studies included in the review were single studies with small sample sizes and limited events, which reduces the reliability of the findings. 11. The question under investigation is whether isopropyl alcohol scrub combined with an iodophor-impregnated antimicrobial skin sealant is more effective than iodophor scrub alone in preventing infections following cesarean sections. 12. The setting for the studies reviewed is hospitals in the United States. 13. The evidence certainty for the interventions is rated as very low due to methodological limitations, including small sample sizes and few or no events in some studies. 14. WHO recommendations emphasize the choice of antiseptic agent and method of application for preoperative skin preparation in cesarean sections. 15. Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHX) was compared to povidone-iodine (PVP-I) in eight trials involving 4,323 women. 16. One trial compared 3% CHX plus 3% cetrimide scrub followed by 95% isopropyl alcohol scrub to 10% PVP-I paint, with no significant differences described. 17. The studies reviewed include various methods of application and concentrations of antiseptic agents, but detailed descriptions are often lacking. 18. The references cited include systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, and WHO guidelines on surgical site infection prevention and antiseptic use. 19. The studies highlight the importance of infection control practices in maternity units and their impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes. 20. The findings underscore the need for further research to establish the most effective antiseptic agents and methods for preoperative skin preparation in cesarean sections.
